artifacts.summary: Five-phase, 3-hour plan routing lean-sorry-census.sh --cross-check through the lake build guard with a test-seam env var and three-way graceful degradation, recording the no-hook decision, and rewriting multi-instance-optimization.md as mechanism documentation with corrected memory figures.

memory_candidates.content: Cross-extension script dependency in this agent system: extension scripts from DIFFERENT source-store extensions (agent-system/extensions/<ext>/scripts/) deploy FLAT into a single .claude/scripts/ directory, so they are siblings only post-deploy. A script in extension A invoking a script from extension B must therefore resolve it via $(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-$0}")/<name>.sh, which is correct and CWD-independent post-deploy but always fails when the script is exercised directly from the source store -- which is exactly how the test suites invoke it. The resolution is an overridable env-var test seam, `:-`-defaulted to the dirname-relative sibling (precedent: LAKE_BUILD_GUARD_LAKE_BIN in lake-build-guard.sh), letting tests inject a stub without a real toolchain. Related: extension lifecycle hooks are NOT a substitute for this wiring -- skill_get_extension_dir keys hook resolution strictly on task_type, so an extension's hook never fires for general/meta-typed tasks touching that extension's files, and hooks are non-blocking by design (non-zero exit downgraded to a WARNING), so they can detect but never enforce.
